paper.title_en: Investigating the Neupert Effect with HEL1OS/Aditya-L1
paper.abstract_en: We investigate the Neupert effect in solar flares using broadband hard X-ray observations from the HEL1OS instrument onboard Aditya-L1. By separating thermal and non-thermal components from HEL1OS spectrograms, we analyse a sample of 312 flares observed between November 2023 and May 2026. We find that the soft X-ray flux is strongly correlated with the time-integrated hard X-ray emission, with a median correlation coefficient of 0.984, indicating that Neupert-like behaviour is nearly ubiquitous in flares with detectable non-thermal emission. Extending beyond statistical correlation, we develop an empirical forward model in which the thermal lightcurve is reconstructed from the non-thermal emission by resolving the hard X-ray lightcurve into individual energy-release episodes and convolving their fitted profiles with finite thermal-response functions. This approach successfully reproduces the observed thermal evolution, including flares that exhibit quasi-periodic pulsations (QPPs). Our results demonstrate that the broadband HEL1OS observations sample both thermal-dominated and non-thermal-dominated flare emission within a single instrument, providing an observation-driven link between the temporal structure of non-thermal HXR emission and the thermal X-ray response. This provides a different framework for interpreting flare energetics and temporal evolution using broadband hard X-ray measurements.
